principles.text: A stock that gaps down (or opens) into rising EMAs (support) is a much safer, higher-odds entry than one gapping up into a declining EMA or overhead resistance — the latter has a much higher chance of getting rejected and reversing.

Set your stop well below resistance rather than entering right at the highs into that resistance — that way even a mild pullback doesn't stop you out, whereas entering at the highs means normal chop can shake you out before the move even starts.
It's never wrong to book some profits and sell into strength, especially once a position is extended from a key moving average and approaching a prior swing high.
Small/micro caps are hard to trade and prone to shakeouts and fakeouts; with enough liquid, high-ADR mid-cap-and-above names available, there's no need to bother trading small caps.
The best pullback entries are the ones where multiple support levels — e.g. weekly 9 EMA, daily 9/21 EMA, 1-hour 50 EMA, and the prior breakout area — all converge at the same price.

Stops are only executed at the open, not pre-market or after-hours — if a stock gaps below the stop overnight, he lets it happen and reassesses the position/stop at the open rather than acting on the pre-market print.

Tightening a stop (holding all else equal) doesn't inherently change a trade's expectancy on its own, but in his experience the larger risk-multiple gained from a tighter stop tends to outweigh the decrease in win rate, because good trades rarely pull back more than ~1-1.5% before continuing in his favor.

There's no single best or 'magical' approach that works for everyone in trading; learn from what other traders share, but adapt or discard it based on what actually works for you rather than copying it 100%.

Avoids running a trading community/Discord because roughly 95% of trader-to-trader discussion is noise from people still in their learning phase; only a small fraction of experienced, profitable traders are actively engaged in group discussions.
Less screen time can be a net positive — you'll miss some trades, but you also cut out boredom trades and revenge trades, and can hold positions for longer.
